For a shared edge with distinct endpoints p and q, the outward face restrictions are reversed maps, γ(t)=q_a((1−t)p+tq) and γ(1−t); they differ at t=0 because q_a(p)≠q_a(q), so they are distinct chain generators and do not cancel. Thus z is not a smooth singular cycle. The example’s flux definition and the cited nonzero-period obstruction in `thm-emx-local-potential-homotopy` require a cycle, so that argument does not establish the no-potential conclusion.
